passages.text: Wang did not attend university; he began his career in print and dyeing factories in Shunde, Guangdong, a manufacturing hub with easy river access to Hong Kong, where factories needed to get samples to Hong Kong-based buyers quickly -- a logistical need that led to SF Express's founding in the early 1990s.
Wang moved to Hong Kong with his family at age 7 and attended primary and secondary school there before returning to work in Guangdong's manufacturing sector.

SF Holding founder Wang Wei was separately appointed as a non-executive director to the board of J&T Global Express, a rival logistics company, according to reporting cited in search results (not independently fetched in full in this pass).
Founded SF Express in the early 1990s to provide express delivery between Guangdong manufacturers and Hong Kong buyers.

SF Express grew into SF Holding, a major Shenzhen-based multinational logistics conglomerate, with Wang remaining chairman and majority shareholder and an estimated net worth of $15.3 billion as of August 2026 per Wikipedia.

Wang-wei-sf-express belongs to Group 4 - Mobile/e-commerce. The mobile/e-commerce group covers founders who built the smartphone-era platforms of the 2010s — ride-hailing (Didi), social commerce (Pinduoduo), local services (Meituan), short video (Kuaishou), logistics (SF Express, ZTO), and e-commerce at scale (JD.com) — a cohort whose businesses were shaped by the mobile-internet transition and, for several, by the 2020-2021 regulatory tightening.
